shape.title: Shapes
shape.intro: A shape is a figure with a specific form. Shapes are all around us!
shape.example3: Triangles (like road signs, pizza slices, roofs)

circle.title: Circle
circle.intro: A circle is a round shape where every point is the same distance from the center.
circle.centerDesc: The middle point of the circle
circle.radiusDesc: The distance from the center to any point on the circle
circle.diameterDesc: The distance across the circle through the center (Diameter = 2 × Radius)

rectangle.title: Rectangle
rectangle.intro: A rectangle is a four-sided shape with opposite sides equal and all corners at 90 degrees.

square.title: Square
square.intro: A square is a special rectangle where all four sides are equal.
square.special: Think of a square as a rectangle where length = width!

triangle.title: Triangle
triangle.intro: A triangle is a shape with three sides and three corners (angles).

line.title: Lines, Rays, and Line Segments
line.intro: Understanding the basic building blocks of geometry:
line.pointDesc: An exact location in space (shown as a dot)
line.lineSegmentDesc: A straight path between two points (has two endpoints)
line.rayDesc: Starts at one point and goes on forever in one direction (has one endpoint)

angle.title: Angles
angle.intro: An angle is formed when two rays or line segments meet at a point. We measure angles in degrees (°).
angle.right: Right Angle: Exactly 90° (like a corner of a square)
angle.obtuse: Obtuse Angle: More than 90° but less than 180° (wide angle)

squareVsRectangle.title: Square vs Rectangle
squareVsRectangle.point1: Every square is a rectangle (it has 4 sides and 4 right angles)
squareVsRectangle.point2: Not every rectangle is a square (only if all sides are equal)

example1.title: Finding the Diameter
example1.question: A circle has a radius of 5 cm. What is its diameter?

example2.title: Identifying Triangle Types
example2.question: A triangle has sides of length 7 cm, 7 cm, and 5 cm. What type of triangle is it?
example2.step1: Count how many sides are equal: Two sides are 7 cm
example2.step2: When exactly 2 sides are equal, it's an isosceles triangle

example3.title: Identifying Angles
example3.question: Look at the corner of a piece of paper. What type of angle is it?
example3.step1: The corner of paper forms a perfect square corner

exercise1.question: If the radius of a circle is 8 inches, what is the diameter?

exercise2.question: How many sides does a square have?
exercise2.hint: Count the sides of a square shape

exercise3.question: Which triangle has all three sides of different lengths?
exercise3.explanation: A scalene triangle has all three sides of different lengths

exercise4.question: How many degrees are in a right angle?
exercise4.hint: Think of the corner of a square
exercise4.explanation: A right angle is exactly 90 degrees

exercise5.question: An angle that measures 45° is called:
exercise5.explanation: An acute angle is any angle less than 90°. Since 45° < 90°, it's acute

basicShapes.title: Basic Shapes
basicShapes.caption: The four fundamental shapes you should know

circleParts.title: Parts of a Circle
circleParts.caption: Diameter is always twice the radius

rectangleSquare.title: Rectangle vs Square
rectangleSquare.caption: A square is a special type of rectangle

notes.tip1: Look around your room! Can you find circles, squares, rectangles, and triangles? Geometry is everywhere!
notes.trick1: Memory trick: A SQUARE has EQUAL sides. Both words have 'QUA' in them!
notes.warning1: Don't confuse the names! Equilateral = all equal, Isosceles = two equal, Scalene = all different (no equal sides)
notes.tip2: To remember angle types: Acute is 'a-cute' (small) angle, Obtuse sounds like 'obese' (big) angle!

conclusion.title: Excellent Work!
conclusion.summary: You've learned the basics of geometry! These shapes and concepts are the foundation for understanding the world around you.
conclusion.takeaway1: Shapes have specific properties: circles are round, rectangles have 4 right angles, triangles have 3 sides
conclusion.takeaway2: A square is a special rectangle where all sides are equal
conclusion.takeaway3: Triangles are classified by their sides: equilateral (all equal), isosceles (2 equal), scalene (all different)
conclusion.takeaway4: Angles come in different types: right (90°), acute (<90°), obtuse (>90°), and straight (180°)
